name: ISO 19650 UK-style project standard (architecture and interiors, metric)
description: A starting project standard in the style of UK public-sector ISO 19650 practice: Uniclass-classified layer names in the ISO 13567 field order used by the DfE Projects Information Standard, ISO 19650-2 UK National Annex container names, suitability and revision codes, metric scales and plotted text heights. Built from public guidance; it is not the text of ISO 19650, ISO 13567 or the National Annex.
jurisdiction: United Kingdom (style preset; not a code or a licensed standard)
notes: STATUS: style preset. ISO 13567, ISO 19650-2 and its UK National Annex are paywalled; nothing here is presented as their official content. Sources: UK Department for Education Projects Information Standard (ER-DFE-XX-XX-T-X-0003 C01), which states it is aligned to BS EN ISO 19650-2 NA incl. the Feb 2021 corrigendum [S14]; UK BIM Framework Guidance Part C [S15]; Symetri [S17]; Wikipedia ISO 13567 [S12]; Wikipedia ISO 216 [N06]; ISO 128-20 sample pages [N05]; ISO 3098 sample pages [S80, search excerpt]; Uniclass 2015 online tables, NBS (uniclass.thenbs.com; Systems table v1.44 and CAD table v1.3, read 2026-11-27). Source ids resolve in references/practice/_SOURCES.md and research/05-expert-practice-and-standards.md.

LAYER SCHEME CHOSEN, AND WHY: Uniclass-style names in ISO 13567 field order, exactly as DfE specifies: Agent (discipline code followed by '-'), Element (Uniclass code truncated to 6 characters with underscores removed: Ss_25_10_20 -> Ss2510), Presentation ('--'), Description (Uniclass title in PascalCase): A-Ss2510--CurtainWallingSystems, S-Ss2030--Columns [S14]. DfE requires DWG and IFC outputs to conform to BS EN ISO 13567-2 [S14]. The full 9-field ISO 13567 form (status, sector, phase, projection, scale, work package) was NOT used: its field lengths are known only from a secondary summary of the paywalled text [S12] and no public source gives its presentation or status code letters, so a checker built on it would enforce unsourced codes. The DfE form was read first-hand, is current UK public-sector practice and uses a free classification (Uniclass).

HOW THE SCHEME IS ENCODED: filler '-' (DfE pads with '-'), case 'any' (Uniclass codes are mixed case). Field agent (2, required) uses codeList disciplines. Field element (6, required) is matched by PREFIX against the Uniclass tables usable for layers (EF, Ss, Pr, SL, Zz): this validates the table prefix and shape, NOT that the numeric code exists in Uniclass; that check is PARTIAL. Field presentation (2) is optional because DfE always writes '--'. The description is the user-defined part. Uniclass codes shorter than 6 characters are padded with the filler: Zz_90 -> Zz90--.

STATUS AND PHASE IN LAYER NAMES: the DfE form has no status field. Projects that need new/existing/demolish layers should add a suffix to the description (for example ...Existing, ...Demolish) and list those layers; this preset does not invent status letters.

CONTAINER NAMES (fileNaming) [S14][S17]: Project-Originator-Functional breakdown-Spatial breakdown-Form-Discipline-Number, hyphen reserved as separator. Originator 3 characters; functional and spatial breakdown 2 characters each (ZZ multiple, XX none, 00 site, 01... buildings or levels); Form from NA.3.6 (codeList forms, COMPLETE per DfE); Discipline from NA.3.7 (codeList disciplines, COMPLETE per DfE; I, J, K are DfE allocations of NA spare codes; spare N, U, V are omitted); Number exactly 4 digits (DfE project rule). The project code length is not fixed by the source; [A-Z0-9]+ is a default. Status and revision are metadata, not part of the name, except for files held outside the CDE, where DfE appends description, suitability and revision (example 3) [S14][S21]; the optional trailing fields model that. Projects on the 2018 NA field names use two-character Type codes (DR, M3) and Role [S17][S83]; the full legacy Type and Role lists were NOT found in a public source, so they are not included.

SHEET NUMBERS: DfE puts the full container name in the drawing number [S14], so sheetNumbering is the container name without extension and with Form = D (drawing). Projects that number sheets by a short code should replace this rule.

SUITABILITY (statusCodes) [S15] Table 2, NA Table NA.1: COMPLETE for S0-S4, S6, S7 and CR; S5 is withdrawn and omitted. A and B codes are numbered per project (A1, An / B1, Bn); A1 and B1 are listed and patterns.suitability accepts any number. Clients redefine codes (DfE redefines S4 and S5 and adds stage-linked A0-A6, B0-B5) [S14]: edit the project copy.
REVISIONS [S15] NA.4.3: P01.01 work in progress (preliminary revision and version), P01 shared, C01 published (contractual) [S15][S14].

SCALES: 1:100 shape and layout; 1:50 junctions; 1:20, 1:10, 1:5 and 1:2 assembly details; models at 1:1 [S14]. 1:200, 1:500, 1:1250 for site plans are typical practice (sheets-sets.md section 6), not sourced.

PLOTTED TEXT HEIGHTS: 1.8 and 2.5 mm general text, dimensions and notes; 3.5 mm sub-headings; 5 mm titles and drawing numbers; 7 mm major titles, Arial [S14]. 10, 14, 20 mm complete the ISO 3098 series [S80, search excerpt only]. Text must stay legible when printed reduced to A3 [S14]: check 1.8 mm text on A1 sheets.

LINEWEIGHTS: every starter layer uses a value of the ISO 128-20 series 0.13, 0.18, 0.25, 0.35, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0 mm [N05]; which value each layer gets follows drawing-conventions.md section 2.2 (typical practice) and is a DEFAULT. Colours are DEFAULTS chosen so one colour maps to one series width (8 0.13, 1 0.18, 3 0.25, 4 0.35, 2 0.5, 6 0.7, 5 1.0); codeLists.plotColours is that default map, not a sourced pen table.

SENSIBLE DEFAULTS, NOT SOURCED (a project should override them): the starter layer selection, all colours, linetypes and lineweight assignments, text and dimension style names and settings other than 2.5 mm dimension text and Arial [S14], title block field names, patterns, codeLists.xrefLayers and codeLists.plotColours.

SHEET SIZES: codeLists.sheetSizes lists ISO A0-A4 in millimetres (width x height, portrait) [N06]. A sizes keep the root-2 ratio, so A1 printed on A3 is exactly half scale [N06]. The schema has no numeric sheet size member, so the size is in each code's name.

UNICLASS TITLES used in layer descriptions were read from the NBS Uniclass browser on 2026-11-27 (Systems v1.44, CAD v1.3). Zz_90 'Readme and plotting lines' is used for non-plotting content; NBS shows its child codes as not in use, so only the group code is used.

LAYER ROLES, VIEW NAMES, PURGE AND TITLE BLOCK: layerRoles names the layer for viewport frames, xref inserts and the title block insert; viewNaming is the view name rule (the same default as patterns.viewName); purge.keep lists names a purge must keep beyond what the standard already lists, and is empty here; titleBlock.blockName and titleBlock.familyType are not set, because the title block is the project's own. All four are DEFAULTS, not sourced: a project sets its own.
